NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to modify the startup/shutdown gas flow sequence to include a controlled re-oxidation stage with humidified N₂ before full re-oxidation, preventing sudden nickel phase expansion. Standard practice uses fixed H₂ flow during startup and N₂ purge during shutdown without controlled re-oxidation. Our mitigation introduces a novel gas sequencing protocol that manages the redox equilibrium by allowing gradual re-oxidation via humidified N₂, which is a departure from abrupt gas switches. The closest existing practice is standard inert gas purging, but our method differs by introducing a controlled partial re-oxidation phase with humidity to modulate nickel oxidation kinetics, not just inert purging.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the volumetric expansion strain ΔV/V = αΔC, where α is the molar expansion coefficient of Ni (≈0.066 mol⁻¹) and ΔC is the change in oxygen concentration. By limiting ΔC through controlled humidified N₂ (H₂O content ≈3% vol), we cap the instantaneous ΔC at ≈0.005 mol (vs. 0.03 mol in dry air), reducing peak strain by 83% and keeping interfacial stress below the fracture threshold (σ < 100 MPa). This prevents microstructural rearrangement and agglomeration.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- (a) Modify existing flow controller logic (anode H₂ inlet) — implement a 3-stage startup sequence: Stage 1 (30s): H₂ at 0.2 L/min with 5% H₂O vapor; Stage 2 (60s): H₂ at 0.3 L/min with 3% H₂O vapor; Stage 3 (90s): Full H₂ flow at 0.5 L/min (no H₂O).  
- (a) Modify existing flow controller logic (anode N₂ inlet) — implement a 2-stage shutdown sequence: Stage 1 (60s): N₂ at 0.5 L/min with 3% H₂O vapor; Stage 2 (30s): Full N₂ purge at 1 L/min (no H₂O).  
- (b) Procure a standard commercial humidifier (e.g., Perma Pure HUM-1) to add H₂O vapor to the H₂/N₂ streams (max flow 1 L/min, compatible with 750°C).  
- (b) Procure a standard commercial temperature/humidity sensor (e.g., Sensirion SHT85) to monitor inlet stream humidity (calibrated for 0–5% H₂O range).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —  
- Installation: Standard practice requires flow controller logic modification (0.5 labor hr). Proposed adds humidifier/sensor installation (1.0 labor hr), but no new tooling or requalification — burden class same.  
- Commissioning: Standard practice requires gas sequence validation (1.0 hr). Proposed adds humidity calibration (0.5 hr), but total time within 20% of standard — burden class same.  
- Operation: Standard practice uses existing gas flows. Proposed adds humidity monitoring (no operator action) — burden class same.  
- Maintenance: Standard practice requires periodic flow calibration. Proposed adds humidity sensor recalibration (every 6 mo, same as standard practice) — burden class same.  
- Cost: Humidifier/sensor are standard catalog items ($500 total), within the existing instrumentation budget class — burden class same.  

EXECUTABLE TEST —  
- Protocol: Subject cells to 200 start-stop cycles at 750°C with the proposed gas sequence. Measure interfacial stress via in-situ curvature monitoring (laser deflection) and track power density at 0.7 V.  
- Instruments: Laser deflection system (stress resolution ±5 MPa), electrochemical analyzer (power density resolution ±0.01 W/cm²), humidity sensor (±0.1% H₂O).  
- Pass/Fail: Pass if interfacial stress < 100 MPa at all cycles and power density > 0.35 W/cm² after 200 cycles. Fail if stress exceeds 100 MPa or power density drops below 0.35 W/cm².  
- Duration: 200 cycles (≈1 month accelerated testing at 750°C).  
- Kill Criterion: Immediate failure if interfacial stress exceeds 150 MPa (indicating imminent cracking).
